title: Writing to a file on a disk
question: The same write, on ext4: is anything written to the disk?
text: The same write as in memory, but on ext4. Is anything written to the disk?

[ext4_buffered_write_iter](2:ext4_buffered_write_iter) puts the bytes into the page cache, as in memory, and marks the page dirty: to be written back later. [ext4_da_write_begin](2:ext4_da_write_begin) is delayed allocation: no disk block is chosen for the data yet, one is only reserved. So nothing reaches the disk in this call; that happens in writeback, or in fsync (the next example).
Try: [open with O_SYNC](try:1): the write itself then has to reach the disk, and the run grows by the whole writeback path.
tries: int fd = openat(AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/new.txt", O_CREAT | O_WRONLY | O_SYNC, 0644); write(fd, "hello, ext4\n", 12); close(fd)
